texts.text: Precautions to be taken before handling or administering the medicinal product
texts.label: text

texts.text: CRESEMBA must be reconstituted and then further diluted to a concentration corresponding to a range of 0.4 to 0.8 mg/mL isavuconazole prior to administration by intravenous infusion over a minimum of 1 hour to reduce the risk of infusion-related reactions. Higher concentrations should be avoided as these may cause local irritation at the site of infusion. The infusion must be administered via an infusion set with an in-line filter with a microporous membrane made of polyethersulfone (PES) and with a pore size of 0.2 μm to 1.2 μm. CRESEMBA must only be given as an intravenous infusion.

texts.text: 4.4 Special warnings and precautions for use
texts.label: text

texts.text: Hypersensitivity
texts.label: text

texts.text: Hypersensitivity to isavuconazole may result in adverse reactions that include: anaphylactic reaction, hypotension, respiratory failure, dyspnoea, drug eruption, pruritus, and rash (see section 4.8). In case of anaphylactic reaction, isavuconazole should be discontinued immediately and appropriate medical treatment should be initiated.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Caution should be used in prescribing isavuconazole to patients with hypersensitivity to other azole antifungal agents.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Infusion-related reactions
texts.label: text

texts.text: During intravenous administration of isavuconazole, infusion-related reactions including hypotension, dyspnoea, dizziness, paraesthesia, nausea, and headache were reported (see section 4.8). The infusion should be stopped if these reactions occur.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions
texts.label: text

texts.text: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions, such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome, have been reported during treatment with azole antifungal agents. If a patient develops a severe cutaneous adverse reaction, CRESEMBA should be discontinued.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Cardiovascular
texts.label: text

texts.text: QT shortening
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is contraindicated in patients with familial short QT syndrome (see section 4.3). In a QT study in healthy human subjects, isavuconazole shortened the QTc interval in a concentration-related manner. For the 200 mg dosing regimen, the least squares mean (LSM) difference from placebo was 13.1 ms at 2 hours post dose [90% CI: 17.1, 9.1 ms]. Increasing the dose to 600 mg resulted in an LSM difference from placebo of 24.6 ms at 2 hours post dose [90% CI: 28.7, 20.4 ms].
texts.label: text

texts.text: Caution is warranted when prescribing isavuconazole to patients taking other medicinal products known to decrease the QT interval, such as rufinamide.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Elevated liver transaminases or hepatitis
texts.label: text

texts.text: Elevated liver transaminases have been reported in clinical studies (see section 4.8). The elevations in liver transaminases rarely required discontinuation of isavuconazole. Monitoring of hepatic enzymes should be considered, as clinically indicated. Hepatitis has been reported with azole antifungal agents including isavuconazole.
texts.label: text

texts.label: text

texts.text: CYP3A4/5 substrates including immunosuppressants
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole can be considered a moderate inhibitor of CYP3A4/5, and systemic exposure to medicinal products metabolised by CYP3A4 may be increased when co-administered with isavuconazole. Concomitant use of isavuconazole with CYP3A4 substrates such as the immunosuppressants tacrolimus, sirolimus or ciclosporin may increase the systemic exposure to these medicinal products. Appropriate therapeutic drug monitoring and dose adjustment may be necessary during co-administration (see section

texts.text: CYP2B6 substrates
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is an inducer of CYP2B6. Systemic exposure to medicinal products metabolised by CYP2B6 may be decreased when co-administered with isavuconazole. Therefore, caution is advised when CYP2B6 substrates, especially medicinal products with a narrow therapeutic index such as cyclophosphamide, are co-administered with isavuconazole. The use of the CYP2B6 substrate efavirenz with isavuconazole is contraindicated because efavirenz is a moderate inducer of CYP3A4/5 (see section

texts.text: P-gp substrates
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole may increase the exposure of medicinal products that are P-gp substrates. Dose adjustment of medicinal products that are P-gp substrates, especially medicinal products with a narrow therapeutic index such as digoxin, colchicine and dabigatran etexilate, may be needed when concomitantly administered with isavuconazole (see section

texts.text: Limitations of the clinical data
texts.label: text

texts.text: The clinical data for isavuconazole in the treatment of mucormycosis are limited to one prospective non-controlled clinical study in 37 adult patients with proven or probable mucormycosis who received isavuconazole for primary treatment, or because other antifungal treatments (predominantly amphotericin B) were inappropriate.
texts.label: text

texts.text: For individual Mucorales species, the clinical efficacy data are very limited, often to one or two patients (see section 5.1). Susceptibility data were available in only a small subset of cases. These data indicate that concentrations of isavuconazole required for inhibition in vitro are very variable between genera/species within the order of Mucorales , and generally higher than concentrations required to inhibit Aspergillus species. It should be noted that there was no dose-finding study in mucormycosis, and patients were administered the same dose of isavuconazole as was used for the treatment of invasive aspergillosis.
texts.label: text

texts.text: 4.5 Interaction with other medicinal products and other forms of interaction
texts.label: text

texts.text: Potential of medicinal products to affect the pharmacokinetics of isavuconazole
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is a substrate of CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 (see section 5.2). Co-administration of medicinal products which are inhibitors of CYP3A4 and/or CYP3A5 may increase the plasma concentrations of isavuconazole. Co-administration of medicinal products which are inducers of CYP3A4 and/or CYP3A5 may decrease the plasma concentrations of isavuconazole.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Medicinal products that inhibit CYP3A4/5
texts.label: text

texts.text: Co-administration of isavuconazole with the strong CYP3A4/5 inhibitor ketoconazole is contraindicated, since this medicinal product can significantly increase plasma concentrations of isavuconazole (see sections 4.3 and
texts.label: text

texts.text: For the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor lopinavir/ritonavir, a two-fold increase in isavuconazole exposure was observed. For other strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as clarithromycin, indinavir and saquinavir, a less pronounced effect can be expected, based on their relative potency. No dose adjustment of isavuconazole is necessary when co-administered with strong CYP3A4/5 inhibitors, however caution is advised as adverse drug reactions may increase (see section
texts.label: text

texts.text: No dose adjustment is warranted for moderate to mild CYP3A4/5 inhibitors.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Medicinal products that induce CYP3A4/5
texts.label: text

texts.text: Co-administration of isavuconazole with potent CYP3A4/5 inducers such as rifampicin, rifabutin, carbamazepine, long-acting barbiturates (e.g., phenobarbital), phenytoin and St. John’s wort, or with moderate CYP3A4/5 inducers such as efavirenz, nafcillin and etravirine, is contraindicated, since these medicinal products can significantly decrease plasma concentrations of isavuconazole (see section
texts.label: text

texts.label: text

texts.text: Medicinal products metabolised by CYP3A4/5
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is a moderate inhibitor of CYP3A4/5; co-administration of isavuconazole with medicinal products which are substrates of CYP3A4/5 may result in increased plasma concentrations of these medicinal products.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Medicinal products metabolised by CYP2B6
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is a mild CYP2B6 inducer; co-administration of isavuconazole may result in decreased plasma concentrations of CYP2B6 substrates.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Medicinal products transported by P-gp in the intestine
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is a mild inhibitor of P-glycoprotein (P-gp); co-administration with isavuconazole may result in increased plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Medicinal products transported by BCRP
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is an inhibitor in vitro of BCRP, and plasma concentrations of substrates of BCRP may therefore be increased. Caution is advised when isavuconazole is given concomitantly with substrates of BCRP.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Medicinal products renally excreted via transport proteins
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is a mild inhibitor of the organic cation transporter 2 (OCT2). Co-administration of isavuconazole with medicinal products which are substrates of OCT2 may result in increased plasma concentrations of these medicinal products.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Uridine diphosphate-glucuronosyltransferases (UGT) substrates
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is a mild inhibitor of UGT. Co-administration of isavuconazole with medicinal products which are substrates of UGT may result in mildly increased plasma concentrations of these medicinal products.
texts.label: text

texts.text: 4.7 Effects on ability to drive and use machines
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole has a moderate potential to influence the ability to drive and use machines. Patients should avoid driving or operating machinery if symptoms of confusional state, somnolence, syncope, and/or dizziness are experienced.

texts.label: text

texts.text: In a double-blind, randomized, active-controlled clinical study of 516 patients with invasive fungal disease caused by Aspergillus species or other filamentous fungi, elevated liver transaminases (alanine aminotransferase or aspartate aminotransferase) > 3 × Upper Limit of Normal (ULN) were reported at the end of study treatment in 4.4% of patients who received isavuconazole. texts.text: Paediatric population
texts.label: text

texts.text: The clinical safety of isavuconazole was assessed in 77 paediatric patients who received at least one dose of intravenous or oral isavuconazole. This included 46 paediatric patients who received isavuconazole as a single dose and who also received other antifungals for prophylaxis, and 31 patients with suspected or confirmed invasive aspergillosis or mucormycosis who received isavuconazole as primary therapy for up to 181 days. Overall, the safety profile of isavuconazole in the paediatric population was similar to that in adults.

texts.text: 4.9 Overdose
texts.label: text

texts.text: Symptoms
texts.label: text

texts.text: Symptoms reported more frequently at supratherapeutic doses of isavuconazole (equivalent to isavuconazole 600 mg/day) evaluated in a QT study than in the therapeutic dose group (equivalent to isavuconazole 200 mg/day dose) included: headache, dizziness, paraesthesia, somnolence, disturbance in attention, dysgeusia, dry mouth, diarrhoea, oral hypoaesthesia, vomiting, hot flush, anxiety, restlessness, palpitations, tachycardia, photophobia and arthralgia.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Management of overdose
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is not removed by haemodialysis. There is no specific antidote for isavuconazole. In the event of an overdose, supportive treatment should be instituted.
texts.label: text

texts.text: 5. PHARMACOLOGICAL PROPERTIES
texts.label: text

texts.text: 5.1 Pharmacodynamic properties
texts.label: text

texts.text: Pharmacotherapeutic group: Antimycotics for systemic use, triazole- and tetrazole derivative, ATC code: J02AC05.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Mechanism of action
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is the active moiety formed after oral or intravenous administration of isavuconazonium sulfate (see section
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole demonstrates a fungicidal effect by blocking the synthesis of ergosterol, a key component of the fungal cell membrane, through the inhibition of cytochrome P-450-dependent enzyme lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, responsible for the conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol. This results in an accumulation of methylated sterol precursors and a depletion of ergosterol within the cell membrane, thus weakening the structure and function of the fungal cell membrane.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Microbiology
texts.label: text

texts.text: In animal models of disseminated and pulmonary aspergillosis, the pharmacodynamic (PD) index important in efficacy is exposure divided by minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) (AUC/MIC). No clear correlation between in vitro MIC and clinical response for the different species ( Aspergillus and Mucorales ) could be established.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Concentrations of isavuconazole required to inhibit Aspergillus species and genera/species of the order Mucorales in vitro have been very variable. Generally, concentrations of isavuconazole required to inhibit Mucorales are higher than those required to inhibit the majority of Aspergillus species.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Clinical efficacy has been demonstrated for the following Aspergillus species: Aspergillus fumigatus , A. flavus , A. niger , and A. terreus (see further below).
texts.label: text

texts.text: Mechanism(s) of resistance
texts.label: text

texts.text: Reduced susceptibility to triazole antifungal agents has been associated with mutations in the fungal cyp51A and cyp51B genes coding for the target protein lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase involved in ergosterol biosynthesis. Fungal strains with reduced in vitro susceptibility to isavuconazole have been reported, and cross-resistance with voriconazole and other triazole antifungal agents cannot be excluded.

texts.text: Treatment of invasive aspergillosis
texts.label: text

texts.text: The safety and efficacy of isavuconazole for the treatment of adult patients with invasive aspergillosis was evaluated in a double-blind, active-controlled clinical study in 516 patients with invasive fungal disease caused by Aspergillus species or other filamentous fungi. In the intent-to-treat (ITT) population, 258 patients received isavuconazole and 258 patients received voriconazole.

texts.text: Isavuconazole was administered intravenously (equivalent to 200 mg isavuconazole) every 8 hours for the first 48 hours, followed by once-daily intravenous or oral treatment (equivalent to 200 mg isavuconazole). The protocol-defined maximum treatment duration was 84 days. Median treatment duration was 45 days.

The myITT population comprised 123 patients receiving isavuconazole and 108 patients receiving voriconazole. The overall response in this population was n = 43 (35%) for isavuconazole and n = 42 (38.9%) for voriconazole. texts.text: Treatment of mucormycosis
texts.label: text

texts.text: In an open-label non-controlled study, 37 adult patients with proven or probable mucormycosis received isavuconazole at the same dose regimen as that used to treat invasive aspergillosis. Median treatment duration was 84 days for the overall mucormycosis patient population, and 102 days for the 21 patients not previously treated for mucormycosis. For patients with probable or proven mucormycosis as defined by the independent Data Review Committee (DRC), all-cause mortality at Day 84 was 43.2% (16/37) for the overall patient population, 42.9% (9/21) for mucormycosis patients receiving isavuconazole as primary treatment, and 43.8% (7/16) for mucormycosis patients receiving isavuconazole who were refractory to, or intolerant of, prior antifungal therapy (mainly amphotericin B-based treatments). The DRC-assessed overall success rate at EOT was 11/35 (31.4%), with 5 patients considered completely cured and 6 patients partially cured. A stable response was observed in an additional 10/35 patients (28.6%). In 9 patients with mucormycosis due to Rhizopus spp., 4 patients showed a favourable response to isavuconazole. In 5 patients with mucormycosis due to Rhizomucor spp., no favourable responses were observed. The clinical experience in other species is very limited ( Lichtheimia spp. n=2, Cunninghamella spp. n=1, Actinomucor elegans n=1).

texts.text: Paediatric population
texts.label: text

texts.text: The clinical safety of isavuconazole was assessed in 77 paediatric patients who received at least one dose of intravenous or oral isavuconazole, including 31 paediatric patients who received isavuconazole in a clinical study for treating invasive aspergillosis or mucormycosis. Isavuconazole was safe and well tolerated in the treatment of invasive aspergillosis and mucormycosis at the intended treatment durations.
texts.label: text

texts.text: 5.3 Preclinical safety data
texts.label: text

texts.text: In rats and rabbits, isavuconazole at systemic exposures below the therapeutic level were associated with dose-related increases in the incidence of skeletal anomalies (rudimentary supernumerary ribs) in offspring. In rats, a dose-related increase in the incidence of zygomatic arch fusion was also noted in offspring (see section
texts.label: text

texts.text: Administration of isavuconazonium sulfate to rats at a dose of 90 mg/kg/day (approximately 1.0-fold the systemic exposure at the human clinical maintenance dose of 200 mg isavuconazole) during pregnancy through the weaning period showed an increased perinatal mortality of the pups. In utero exposure to the active moiety isavuconazole had no effect on the fertility or the normal development of the surviving pups.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Intravenous administration of 14 C-labelled isavuconazonium sulfate to lactating rats resulted in the recovery of radiolabel in the milk.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole did not affect the fertility of male or female rats treated with oral doses up to 90 mg/kg/day (approximately 1.0-fold the systemic exposure at the human clinical maintenance dose of 200 mg isavuconazole).
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole has no discernible mutagenic or genotoxic potential. Isavuconazole was negative in a bacterial reverse mutation assay, was weakly clastogenic at cytotoxic concentrations in the L5178Y tk+/- mouse lymphoma chromosome aberration assay, and showed no biologically relevant or statistically significant increase in the frequency of micronuclei in an in vivo rat micronucleus test.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole has demonstrated carcinogenic potential in 2-year rodent carcinogenicity studies. Liver and thyroid tumours are likely caused by a rodent-specific mechanism that is not relevant for humans. Skin fibromas and fibrosarcomas were seen in male rats. The mechanism underlying this effect is unknown. Endometrial adenomas and carcinomas of the uterus were seen in female rats, which is likely due to a hormonal disturbance. There is no safety margin for these effects. The relevance for humans of the skin and uterine tumours cannot be excluded.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole inhibited the hERG potassium channel and the L-type calcium channel with an IC50 of 5.82 µM and 6.57 µM respectively (34- and 38-fold the human non-protein bound Cmax at maximum recommended human dose [MRHD], respectively). The in vivo 39-week repeated-dose toxicology studies in monkeys did not show QTcF prolongation at doses up to 40 mg/kg/day (approximately 1.0-fold the systemic exposure at the human clinical maintenance dose of 200 mg isavuconazole).
texts.label: text

texts.text: Juvenile animal studies
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazonium sulfate, when administered to juvenile rats, demonstrated a similar toxicological profile to that observed in adult animals. In juvenile rats, treatment-related toxicity considered rodent specific was observed in the liver and thyroid. These changes are not considered clinically relevant. Based on the no-observed-adverse-effect level in juvenile rats, the safety margins for isavuconazonium sulfate were approximately 0.2- to 0.5-fold the systemic exposure at the clinical maintenance dose for paediatric patients, similar to those observed in adult rats.

texts.text: Hypersensitivity
texts.label: text

texts.text: Hypersensitivity to isavuconazole may result in adverse reactions that include: anaphylactic reaction, hypotension, respiratory failure, dyspnoea, drug eruption, pruritus, and rash (see section 4.8). In case of anaphylactic reaction, isavuconazole should be discontinued immediately and appropriate medical treatment should be initiated.

texts.text: Caution should be used in prescribing isavuconazole to patients with hypersensitivity to other azole antifungal agents.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions
texts.label: text

texts.text: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions, such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome, have been reported during treatment with azole antifungal agents. If a patient develops a severe cutaneous adverse reaction, CRESEMBA should be discontinued.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Cardiovascular
texts.label: text

texts.text: QT shortening
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is contraindicated in patients with familial short QT syndrome (see section 4.3). In a QT study in healthy human subjects, isavuconazole shortened the QTc interval in a concentration-related manner. For the 200 mg dosing regimen, the least squares mean (LSM) difference from placebo was 13.1 ms at 2 hours post dose [90% CI: 17.1, 9.1 ms]. Increasing the dose to 600 mg resulted in an LSM difference from placebo of 24.6 ms at 2 hours post dose [90% CI: 28.7, 20.4 ms].
texts.label: text

texts.text: Caution is warranted when prescribing isavuconazole to patients taking other medicinal products known to decrease the QT interval, such as rufinamide.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Elevated liver transaminases or hepatitis
texts.label: text

texts.text: Elevated liver transaminases have been reported in clinical studies (see section 4.8). The elevations in liver transaminases rarely required discontinuation of isavuconazole. Monitoring of hepatic enzymes should be considered, as clinically indicated. Hepatitis has been reported with azole antifungal agents including isavuconazole.

texts.text: Limitations of the clinical data
texts.label: text

texts.text: The clinical data for isavuconazole in the treatment of mucormycosis are limited to one prospective non-controlled clinical study in 37 adult patients with proven or probable mucormycosis who received isavuconazole for primary treatment, or because other antifungal treatments (predominantly amphotericin B) were inappropriate.
texts.label: text

texts.text: For individual Mucorales species, the clinical efficacy data are very limited, often to one or two patients (see section 5.1). Susceptibility data were available in only a small subset of cases. These data indicate that concentrations of isavuconazole required for inhibition in vitro are very variable between genera/species within the order of Mucorales , and generally higher than concentrations required to inhibit Aspergillus species. It should be noted that there was no dose-finding study in mucormycosis, and patients were administered the same dose of isavuconazole as was used for the treatment of invasive aspergillosis.

texts.text: Potential of medicinal products to affect the pharmacokinetics of isavuconazole
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is a substrate of CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 (see section 5.2). Co-administration of medicinal products which are inhibitors of CYP3A4 and/or CYP3A5 may increase the plasma concentrations of isavuconazole. Co-administration of medicinal products which are inducers of CYP3A4 and/or CYP3A5 may decrease the plasma concentrations of isavuconazole.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Medicinal products that inhibit CYP3A4/5
texts.label: text

texts.text: Co-administration of isavuconazole with the strong CYP3A4/5 inhibitor ketoconazole is contraindicated, since this medicinal product can significantly increase plasma concentrations of isavuconazole (see sections 4.3 and
texts.label: text

texts.text: For the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor lopinavir/ritonavir, a two-fold increase in isavuconazole exposure was observed. For other strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as clarithromycin, indinavir and saquinavir, a less pronounced effect can be expected, based on their relative potency. No dose adjustment of isavuconazole is necessary when co-administered with strong CYP3A4/5 inhibitors, however caution is advised as adverse drug reactions may increase (see section
texts.label: text

texts.text: No dose adjustment is warranted for moderate to mild CYP3A4/5 inhibitors.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Medicinal products that induce CYP3A4/5
texts.label: text

texts.text: Co-administration of isavuconazole with potent CYP3A4/5 inducers such as rifampicin, rifabutin, carbamazepine, long-acting barbiturates (e.g., phenobarbital), phenytoin and St. John’s wort, or with moderate CYP3A4/5 inducers such as efavirenz, nafcillin and etravirine, is contraindicated, since these medicinal products can significantly decrease plasma concentrations of isavuconazole (see section
texts.label: text

texts.text: Co-administration with mild CYP3A4/5 inducers such as aprepitant, prednisone and pioglitazone, may result in mild to moderate decreases of isavuconazole plasma levels; co-administration with mild CYP3A4/5 inducers should be avoided unless the potential benefit is considered to outweigh the risk (see section
texts.label: text

texts.text: Co-administration with high-dose ritonavir (>200 mg twice daily) is contraindicated, as at high doses ritonavir may induce CYP3A4/5 and decrease isavuconazole plasma concentrations (see section
texts.label: text

texts.text: Potential for isavuconazole to affect exposures of other medicines
texts.label: text

texts.text: Medicinal products metabolised by CYP3A4/5
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is a moderate inhibitor of CYP3A4/5; co-administration of isavuconazole with medicinal products which are substrates of CYP3A4/5 may result in increased plasma concentrations of these medicinal products.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Medicinal products metabolised by CYP2B6
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is a mild CYP2B6 inducer; co-administration of isavuconazole may result in decreased plasma concentrations of CYP2B6 substrates.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Medicinal products transported by P-gp in the intestine
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is a mild inhibitor of P-glycoprotein (P-gp); co-administration with isavuconazole may result in increased plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Medicinal products transported by BCRP
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is an inhibitor in vitro of BCRP, and plasma concentrations of substrates of BCRP may therefore be increased. Caution is advised when isavuconazole is given concomitantly with substrates of BCRP.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Medicinal products renally excreted via transport proteins
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is a mild inhibitor of the organic cation transporter 2 (OCT2). Co-administration of isavuconazole with medicinal products which are substrates of OCT2 may result in increased plasma concentrations of these medicinal products.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Uridine diphosphate-glucuronosyltransferases (UGT) substrates
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is a mild inhibitor of UGT. Co-administration of isavuconazole with medicinal products which are substrates of UGT may result in mildly increased plasma concentrations of these medicinal products.
texts.label: text

texts.text: 4.6 Fertility, pregnancy and lactation
texts.label: text

texts.text: Pregnancy
texts.label: text

texts.text: There are no data from the use of CRESEMBA in pregnant women.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Studies in animals have shown reproductive toxicity (see section 5.3). The potential risk for humans is unknown.
texts.label: text

texts.text: CRESEMBA must not be used during pregnancy except in patients with severe or potentially lifethreatening fungal infections, in whom isavuconazole may be used if the anticipated benefits outweigh the possible risks to the foetus.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Women of child-bearing potential
texts.label: text

texts.text: CRESEMBA is not recommended for women of childbearing potential who are not using contraception.
texts.label: text

texts.label: text

texts.text: Available pharmacodynamic/toxicological data in animals have shown excretion of isavuconazole/metabolites in milk (see section

texts.text: Breast-feeding should be discontinued during treatment with CRESEMBA.

texts.text: 4.7 Effects on ability to drive and use machines
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole has a moderate potential to influence the ability to drive and use machines. Patients should avoid driving or operating machinery if symptoms of confusional state, somnolence, syncope, and/or dizziness are experienced.
texts.label: text

texts.text: 4.8 Undesirable effects
texts.label: text

texts.text: Summary of the safety profile
texts.label: text

texts.text: The most common treatment-related adverse reactions in adults were elevated liver chemistry tests (7.9%), nausea (7.4%), vomiting (5.5%), dyspnoea (3.2%), abdominal pain (2.7%), diarrhoea (2.7%), injection site reaction (2.2%), headache (2.0%), hypokalaemia (1.7%) and rash
texts.label: text

texts.text: The adverse reactions which most often led to permanent discontinuation of isavuconazole treatment in adults were confusional state (0.7%), acute renal failure (0.7%), increased blood bilirubin (0.5%), convulsion (0.5%), dyspnoea (0.5%), epilepsy (0.5%), respiratory failure (0.5%) and vomiting
texts.label: text

texts.text: Tabulated list of adverse reactions
texts.label: text

texts.text: Table 4 presents adverse reactions with isavuconazole in the treatment of invasive fungal infections in adults, by System Organ Class and frequency.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Laboratory effects
texts.label: text

texts.text: In a double-blind, randomized, active-controlled clinical study of 516 patients with invasive fungal disease caused by Aspergillus species or other filamentous fungi, elevated liver transaminases (alanine aminotransferase or aspartate aminotransferase) > 3 × Upper Limit of Normal (ULN) were reported at the end of study treatment in 4.4% of patients who received isavuconazole. texts.text: Paediatric population
texts.label: text

texts.text: The clinical safety of isavuconazole was assessed in 77 paediatric patients who received at least one dose of intravenous or oral isavuconazole. This included 46 paediatric patients who received isavuconazole as a single dose and who also received other antifungals for prophylaxis, and 31 patients with suspected or confirmed invasive aspergillosis or mucormycosis who received isavuconazole as primary therapy for up to 181 days. Overall, the safety profile of isavuconazole in the paediatric population was similar to that in adults.

texts.text: 4.9 Overdose
texts.label: text

texts.text: Symptoms
texts.label: text

texts.text: Symptoms reported more frequently at supratherapeutic doses of isavuconazole (equivalent to isavuconazole 600 mg/day) evaluated in a QT study than in the therapeutic dose group (equivalent to isavuconazole 200 mg/day dose) included: headache, dizziness, paraesthesia, somnolence, disturbance in attention, dysgeusia, dry mouth, diarrhoea, oral hypoaesthesia, vomiting, hot flush, anxiety, restlessness, palpitations, tachycardia, photophobia and arthralgia.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Management of overdose
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is not removed by haemodialysis. There is no specific antidote for isavuconazole. In the event of an overdose, supportive treatment should be instituted.
texts.label: text

texts.text: 5. PHARMACOLOGICAL PROPERTIES
texts.label: text

texts.text: 5.1 Pharmacodynamic properties
texts.label: text

texts.text: Pharmacotherapeutic group: Antimycotics for systemic use, triazole- and tetrazole derivative, ATC code: J02AC05.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Mechanism of action
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole is the active moiety formed after oral or intravenous administration of isavuconazonium sulfate (see section
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole demonstrates a fungicidal effect by blocking the synthesis of ergosterol, a key component of the fungal cell membrane, through the inhibition of cytochrome P-450-dependent enzyme lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, responsible for the conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol. This results in an accumulation of methylated sterol precursors and a depletion of ergosterol within the cell membrane, thus weakening the structure and function of the fungal cell membrane.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Microbiology
texts.label: text

texts.text: In animal models of disseminated and pulmonary aspergillosis, the pharmacodynamic (PD) index important in efficacy is exposure divided by minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) (AUC/MIC). No clear correlation between in vitro MIC and clinical response for the different species ( Aspergillus and Mucorales ) could be established.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Concentrations of isavuconazole required to inhibit Aspergillus species and genera/species of the order Mucorales in vitro have been very variable. Generally, concentrations of isavuconazole required to inhibit Mucorales are higher than those required to inhibit the majority of Aspergillus species.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Clinical efficacy has been demonstrated for the following Aspergillus species: Aspergillus fumigatus , A. flavus , A. niger , and A. terreus (see further below).
texts.label: text

texts.text: Mechanism(s) of resistance
texts.label: text

texts.text: Reduced susceptibility to triazole antifungal agents has been associated with mutations in the fungal cyp51A and cyp51B genes coding for the target protein lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase involved in ergosterol biosynthesis. Fungal strains with reduced in vitro susceptibility to isavuconazole have been reported, and cross-resistance with voriconazole and other triazole antifungal agents cannot be excluded.

texts.text: Treatment of invasive aspergillosis
texts.label: text

texts.text: The safety and efficacy of isavuconazole for the treatment of adult patients with invasive aspergillosis was evaluated in a double-blind, active-controlled clinical study in 516 patients with invasive fungal disease caused by Aspergillus species or other filamentous fungi. In the intent-to-treat (ITT) population, 258 patients received isavuconazole and 258 patients received voriconazole. Isavuconazole was administered intravenously (equivalent to 200 mg isavuconazole) every 8 hours for the first 48 hours, followed by once-daily intravenous or oral treatment (equivalent to 200 mg isavuconazole). The protocol-defined maximum treatment duration was 84 days. Median treatment duration was 45 days.

The myITT population comprised 123 patients receiving isavuconazole and 108 patients receiving voriconazole. texts.text: Treatment of mucormycosis
texts.label: text

texts.text: In an open-label non-controlled study, 37 adult patients with proven or probable mucormycosis received isavuconazole at the same dose regimen as that used to treat invasive aspergillosis. Median treatment duration was 84 days for the overall mucormycosis patient population, and 102 days for the 21 patients not previously treated for mucormycosis. For patients with probable or proven mucormycosis as defined by the independent Data Review Committee (DRC), all-cause mortality at Day 84 was 43.2% (16/37) for the overall patient population, 42.9% (9/21) for mucormycosis patients receiving isavuconazole as primary treatment, and 43.8% (7/16) for mucormycosis patients receiving isavuconazole who were refractory to, or intolerant of, prior antifungal therapy (mainly amphotericin B-based treatments). The DRC-assessed overall success rate at EOT was 11/35 (31.4%), with 5 patients considered completely cured and 6 patients partially cured. A stable response was observed in an additional 10/35 patients (28.6%). In 9 patients with mucormycosis due to Rhizopus spp., 4 patients showed a favourable response to isavuconazole. In 5 patients with mucormycosis due to Rhizomucor spp., no favourable responses were observed. The clinical experience in other species is very limited ( Lichtheimia spp. n=2, Cunninghamella spp. n=1, Actinomucor elegans n=1).
texts.label: text

texts.text: Paediatric population
texts.label: text

texts.text: The clinical safety of isavuconazole was assessed in 77 paediatric patients who received at least one dose of intravenous or oral isavuconazole, including 31 paediatric patients who received isavuconazole in a clinical study for treating invasive aspergillosis or mucormycosis. Isavuconazole was safe and well tolerated in the treatment of invasive aspergillosis and mucormycosis at the intended treatment durations.

texts.label: text

texts.text: In vitro / in vivo studies indicate that CYP3A4, CYP3A5, and subsequently uridine diphosphateglucuronosyltransferases (UGT), are involved in the metabolism of isavuconazole.

texts.text: Following single doses of [cyano14 C] isavuconazonium and [pyridinylmethyl- 14 C] isavuconazonium sulfate in humans, in addition to the active moiety (isavuconazole) and the inactive cleavage product, a number of minor metabolites were identified. Except for the active moiety isavuconazole, no individual metabolite was observed with an AUC > 10% of total radio-labelled material.

texts.label: text

texts.text: 5.3 Preclinical safety data
texts.label: text

texts.text: In rats and rabbits, isavuconazole at systemic exposures below the therapeutic level were associated with dose-related increases in the incidence of skeletal anomalies (rudimentary supernumerary ribs) in offspring. In rats, a dose-related increase in the incidence of zygomatic arch fusion was also noted in offspring (see section
texts.label: text

texts.text: Administration of isavuconazonium sulfate to rats at a dose of 90 mg/kg/day (approximately 1.0-fold the systemic exposure at the human clinical maintenance dose of 200 mg isavuconazole) during pregnancy through the weaning period showed an increased perinatal mortality of the pups. In utero exposure to the active moiety isavuconazole had no effect on the fertility or the normal development of the surviving pups.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Intravenous administration of 14 C-labelled isavuconazonium sulfate to lactating rats resulted in the recovery of radiolabel in the milk.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole did not affect the fertility of male or female rats treated with oral doses up to 90 mg/kg/day (approximately 1.0-fold the systemic exposure at the human clinical maintenance dose of 200 mg isavuconazole).
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole has no discernible mutagenic or genotoxic potential. Isavuconazole was negative in a bacterial reverse mutation assay, was weakly clastogenic at cytotoxic concentrations in the L5178Y tk+/- mouse lymphoma chromosome aberration assay, and showed no biologically relevant or statistically significant increase in the frequency of micronuclei in an in vivo rat micronucleus test.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole has demonstrated carcinogenic potential in 2-year rodent carcinogenicity studies. Liver and thyroid tumours are likely caused by a rodent-specific mechanism that is not relevant for humans. Skin fibromas and fibrosarcomas were seen in male rats. The mechanism underlying this effect is unknown. Endometrial adenomas and carcinomas of the uterus were seen in female rats, which is likely due to a hormonal disturbance. There is no safety margin for these effects. The relevance for humans of the skin and uterine tumours cannot be excluded.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole inhibited the hERG potassium channel and the L-type calcium channel with an IC50 of 5.82 µM and 6.57 µM respectively (34- and 38-fold the human non-protein bound Cmax at maximum recommended human dose [MRHD], respectively). The in vivo 39-week repeated-dose toxicology studies in monkeys did not show QTcF prolongation at doses up to 40 mg/kg/day (approximately 1.0-fold the systemic exposure at the human clinical maintenance dose of 200 mg isavuconazole).
texts.label: text

texts.text: Juvenile animal studies
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazonium sulfate, when administered to juvenile rats, demonstrated a similar toxicological profile to that observed in adult animals. In juvenile rats, treatment-related toxicity considered rodent specific was observed in the liver and thyroid. These changes are not considered clinically relevant. Based on the no-observed-adverse-effect level in juvenile rats, the safety margins for isavuconazonium sulfate were approximately 0.2- to 0.5-fold the systemic exposure at the clinical maintenance dose for paediatric patients, similar to those observed in adult rats.

texts.text: 1. What Cresemba is and what it is used for
texts.label: text

texts.text: What Cresemba is
texts.label: text

texts.text: Cresemba is an anti-fungal medicine that contains the active substance isavuconazole.
texts.label: text

texts.text: How Cresemba works
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole works by killing or stopping the growth of the fungus, which causes the infection.
texts.label: text

texts.text: What Cresemba is used for
texts.label: text

texts.text: Cresemba is used in patients from 1 year of age and older to treat the following fungal infections:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -invasive aspergillosis, caused by a fungus in the 'Aspergillus' group;
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -mucormycosis, caused by a fungus belonging to the 'Mucorales' group in patients for whom a treatment with amphotericin B is not appropriate.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: 2. What you need to know before you use Cresemba
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not use Cresemba:
texts.label: text

texts.text: - if you are allergic to isavuconazole or any of the other ingredients of this medicine (listed in section
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: 6), - if you have a heart beat problem called ‘familial short QT syndrome’,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -if you are using any of the following medicines:
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -ketoconazole, used for fungal infections,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -high doses of ritonavir (more than 200 mg every 12 hours), used for HIV,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -rifampicin, rifabutin, used for tuberculosis,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -carbamazepine, used for epilepsy,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -barbiturate medicines like phenobarbital, used for epilepsy and sleep disorders,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -phenytoin, used for epilepsy,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -St John's wort, a herbal medicine used for depression,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -efavirenz, etravirine, used for HIV,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -nafcillin, used for bacterial infections.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Warnings and precautions
texts.label: text

texts.text: Talk to your doctor, pharmacist or nurse before using Cresemba:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -if you have had an allergic reaction to other 'azole' anti-fungal treatments in the past, such as ketoconazole, fluconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole or posaconazole,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -if you are suffering from severe liver disease. Your doctor should monitor you for possible side effects.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Look out for side effects
texts.label: text

texts.text: Stop using Cresemba and tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following side effects:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -sudden wheezing, difficulty breathing, swelling of the face, lips, mouth or tongue, severe itching, sweating, dizziness or fainting, fast heartbeat or pounding in the chest - these may be signs of a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis).
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Problems while having Cresemba as drip into a vein
texts.label: text

texts.text: Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following side effects:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -low blood pressure, feel short of breath, nausea, dizziness, headache, tingling - your doctor may decide to stop the infusion.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Changes in your liver function
texts.label: text

texts.text: Cresemba can sometimes affect your liver function. Your doctor may carry out blood tests while you are taking this medicine.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Skin problems
texts.label: text

texts.text: Tell your doctor straight away if you get severe blistering of the skin, mouth, eyes or genitals.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Children and adolescents
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not give Cresemba to children younger than 1 year, because there is no information on use in this age group.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Other medicines and Cresemba
texts.label: text

texts.text: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are using, have recently used or might use any other medicines. Some medicines may affect the way Cresemba works or Cresemba may affect the way they work, if they are taken at the same time.
texts.label: text

texts.text: In particular, do not take this medicine and tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking any of the following medicines:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -ketoconazole, used for fungal infections,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -high doses of ritonavir (more than 200 mg every 12 hours), used for HIV,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -rifampicin, rifabutin, used for tuberculosis,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -carbamazepine, used for epilepsy,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -barbiturate medicines like phenobarbital, used for epilepsy and sleep disorders,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -phenytoin, used for epilepsy,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -St John's wort, a herbal medicine used for depression,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -efavirenz, etravirine, used for HIV,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -nafcillin, used for bacterial infections.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Unless your doctor tells you otherwise, do not take this medicine and tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking any of the following medicines:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -rufinamide or other medicines which decrease the QT interval on the heart tracing (ECG),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -aprepitant, used to prevent nausea and vomiting by cancer treatment,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -prednisone, used for rheumatoid arthritis,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -pioglitazone, used for diabetes.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking any of the following medicines, as a dose adjustment or monitoring may be required to check that the medicines are still having the desired effect:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -ciclosporin, tacrolimus and sirolimus, used to prevent rejection of a transplant,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -cyclophosphamide, used for cancer,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -digoxin, used to treat heart failure or an uneven heart beat,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -colchicine, used for gout attack,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -dabigatran etexilate, used to stop blood clots after hip or knee replacement surgery,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -clarithromycin, used for bacterial infections,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -saquinavir, fosamprenavir, indinavir, nevirapine, lopinavir/ritonavir combination, used for HIV,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -alfentanil, fentanyl, used against strong pain,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -vincristine, vinblastine, used for cancer,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), used in transplant patients,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -midazolam, used for severe insomnia and stress,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -bupropion, used for depression,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -metformin, used for diabetes,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -daunorubicin, doxorubicin, imatinib, irinotecan, lapatinib, mitoxantrone, topotecan, used for different sorts of cancer.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Pregnancy and breast-feeding
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you are pregnant or breast-feeding, think you may be pregnant or are planning to have a baby, ask your doctor for advice before using this medicine.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not take Cresemba if you are pregnant, unless your doctor tells you otherwise. This is because it is not known if it may affect or harm your unborn baby.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not breast-feed if you are taking Cresemba.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Driving and using machines
texts.label: text

texts.text: Cresemba may make you feel confused, tired or sleepy. It can also make you pass out. Therefore, be very careful when driving or operating machinery.
texts.label: text

texts.text: 3. How to use Cresemba
texts.label: text

texts.text: Cresemba will be given to you by a doctor or nurse.
texts.label: text

texts.text: The recommended dose is as follows:
texts.label: text

texts.text:

| Adolescents and children with an age from 1 year to less than 18 years |  |  |
| Bodyweight < 37 kg | 5.4 mg/kg isavuconazole | 5.4 mg/kg isavuconazole |
| Bodyweight ≥ 37 kg | 200 mg isavuconazole (one vial) | 200 mg isavuconazole (one vial) |

texts.text: You will be given this dose until your doctor tells you otherwise. The duration of treatment with Cresemba may be longer than 6 months if your doctor considers this necessary.
texts.label: text

texts.text: The vial will be given as a drip into a vein by your doctor or nurse.
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you use more Cresemba than you should
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you think you have been given too much Cresemba, talk to your doctor or nurse straight away. You may have more side effects such as:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -headache, feeling dizzy, restless or sleepy,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -tingling, reduced sense of touch or sensation in the mouth,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -problems being aware of things, hot flushes, anxiety, joint pain,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -changes in the way things taste, dry mouth, diarrhoea, vomiting,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -feeling your heart beat, faster heart rate, being more sensitive to light.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: If you forget to use Cresemba
texts.label: text

texts.text: As you will be given this medicine under close medical supervision, it is unlikely that a dose would be missed. However, tell your doctor or nurse if you think that a dose has been forgotten.
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you stop using Cresemba
texts.label: text

texts.text: Cresemba treatment will continue for as long as your doctor tells you. This is to make sure that the fungal infection has gone.
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you have any further questions on the use of this medicine, ask your doctor, pharmacist or nurse.
texts.label: text

texts.text: 4. Possible side effects
texts.label: text

texts.text: Like all medicines, this medicine can cause side effects, although not everybody gets them.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Stop using Cresemba and tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following side effects:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) such as sudden wheezing, breathing problems, swelling of the face, lips, mouth or tongue, severe itching, sweating, dizziness or fainting, fast heartbeat or pounding in the chest.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following side effects:
texts.label: text

texts.text: Other side effects

texts.text: Tell your doctor, pharmacist or nurse if you notice any of the following side effects:
texts.label: text

texts.text: Common: may affect up to 1 in 10 people
texts.label: text

texts.text: -low potassium in your blood,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -decreased appetite,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -confusion (delirium),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -headache,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -sleepiness,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -inflamed veins that could lead to blood clots,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -shortness of breath or sudden and severe difficulty breathing,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -feeling sick (nausea), being sick (vomiting), diarrhoea, stomach pain,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -changes in blood tests of liver function,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -rash, itching,
texts.label: list_item

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -reduced blood cells called 'platelets' - can increase your risk for bleeding or bruising,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -reduced red blood cells - can make you feel weak or short of breath or make your skin pale,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -severe reduction in blood cells - can make you feel weak, cause bruising or make infections more likely,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -rash, swelling of your lips, mouth, tongue or throat with difficulty breathing (hypersensitivity),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -low blood sugar levels,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -low blood levels of magnesium,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -low levels in the blood of a protein called 'albumin',
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -not getting the right goodness from your diet (malnutrition),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -low blood levels of sodium (hyponatraemia),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -depression, difficulty sleeping,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -seizure, fainting or feeling faint, dizziness,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -sensation of tingling, tickling, or pricking of the skin (paraesthesia),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -altered mental state (encephalopathy),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -changes in taste (dysgeusia),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -feeling of 'spinning' or being dizzy (vertigo),

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -problems with the blood circulation,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -low blood pressure,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -wheezing, very fast breathing, coughing up blood or blood-stained sputum, nose bleeding,

texts.text: -constipation,
texts.label: list_item

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -enlarged liver,

texts.text: Side effects with frequency not known:

texts.text: Reporting of side effects
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you get any side effects, talk to your doctor, pharmacist or nurse. This includes any possible side effects not listed in this leaflet. texts.text: Cresemba 200 mg powder for concentrate for solution for infusion must be reconstituted and diluted prior to infusion.

texts.text: Reconstitution
texts.label: text

texts.text: One vial of the powder for concentrate for solution for infusion should be reconstituted by addition of 5 mL water for injection to the vial. The reconstituted concentrate contains 40 mg isavuconazole per mL. The vial should be shaken to dissolve the powder completely. The reconstituted solution should be inspected visually for particulate matter and discoloration. Reconstituted concentrate should be clear and free of visible particulate. It must be further diluted prior to administration.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Dilution
texts.label: text

texts.text: Adults and paediatric patients with bodyweight from 37 kg:
texts.label: text

texts.text: After reconstitution, the entire content of the reconstituted concentrate should be removed from the vial and added to an infusion bag containing 250 mL of either sodium chloride 9 mg/mL (0.9%) solution for injection or 50 mg/mL (5%) dextrose solution. The infusion solution contains approximately 0.8 mg isavuconazole per mL.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Paediatric patients with bodyweight below 37 kg:
texts.label: text

texts.text: The final concentration of the infusion solution should be in the range of 0.4 to 0.8 mg isavuconazole per mL. Higher concentrations should be avoided as these may cause local irritation at the site of infusion.
texts.label: text

texts.text: To obtain the final concentration, the appropriate volume of the reconstituted concentrate based on paediatric dosing recommendations (see section 3) should be removed from the vial and added to an
texts.label: text

texts.text: infusion bag containing the appropriate amount of diluent. The appropriate volume of the infusion bag is calculated as follows:
texts.label: text

texts.text: [Required dose (mg)/final concentration (mg/mL)] – Volume of the concentrate (mL)
texts.label: text

texts.text: The concentrate can be diluted with either 9 mg/mL (0.9%) sodium chloride solution for injection or 50 mg/mL (5%) dextrose solution.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Administration
texts.label: text

texts.text: After the reconstituted concentrate is further diluted, the diluted solution may show fine white-totranslucent particulates of isavuconazole that do not sediment (but will be removed by in-line filtration). The diluted solution should be mixed gently, or the bag should be rolled to minimise the formation of particulates. Unnecessary vibration or vigorous shaking of the solution should be avoided. The solution for infusion must be administered via an infusion set with an in-line filter (pore size 0.2 μm to 1.2 μm) made of polyether sulfone (PES). Infusion pumps can be used and must be placed before the infusion set. Regardless of the infusion solution container size used, the entire volume of the container should be administered to ensure the complete dose is administered.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole should not be infused into the same line or cannula concomitantly with other intravenous products.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Chemical and physical in-use stability after reconstitution and dilution has been demonstrated for 24 hours at 2 °C to 8 °C, or 6 hours at room temperature.
texts.label: text

texts.text: From a microbiological point of view, the product should be used immediately. If not used immediately, in-use storage times and conditions prior to use are the responsibility of the user and would normally not be longer than 24 hours at 2 °C to 8 °C, unless reconstitution and dilution has taken place in controlled and validated aseptic conditions.
texts.label: text

texts.text: If possible, the intravenous administration of isavuconazole should be completed within 6 hours after reconstitution and dilution at room temperature. If this is not possible, the infusion solution should be immediately refrigerated after dilution, and infusion should be completed within 24 hours.
texts.label: text

texts.text: An existing intravenous line should be flushed with sodium chloride 9 mg/mL (0.9%) solution for injection or 50 mg/mL (5%) dextrose solution.
texts.label: text

texts.text: 1. What Cresemba is and what it is used for
texts.label: text

texts.text: What Cresemba is
texts.label: text

texts.text: Cresemba is an anti-fungal medicine that contains the active substance isavuconazole.
texts.label: text

texts.text: How Cresemba works
texts.label: text

texts.text: Isavuconazole works by killing or stopping the growth of the fungus, which causes the infection.
texts.label: text

texts.text: What Cresemba is used for
texts.label: text

texts.text: Cresemba is used in adults and in paediatric patients from 6 years of age to treat the following fungal infections:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -invasive aspergillosis, caused by a fungus in the 'Aspergillus' group;
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -mucormycosis, caused by a fungus belonging to the 'Mucorales' group in patients for whom a treatment with amphotericin B is not appropriate.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: 2. What you need to know before you take Cresemba
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not take Cresemba:
texts.label: text

texts.text: - if you are allergic to isavuconazole or any of the other ingredients of this medicine (listed in section
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: 6), - if you have a heart beat problem called ‘familial short QT syndrome’,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -if you are using any of the following medicines:
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -ketoconazole, used for fungal infections,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -high doses of ritonavir (more than 200 mg every 12 hours), used for HIV,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -rifampicin, rifabutin, used for tuberculosis,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -carbamazepine, used for epilepsy,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -barbiturate medicines like phenobarbital, used for epilepsy and sleep disorders,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -phenytoin, used for epilepsy,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -St John's wort, a herbal medicine used for depression,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -efavirenz, etravirine, used for HIV,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -nafcillin, used for bacterial infections.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Warnings and precautions
texts.label: text

texts.text: Talk to your doctor, pharmacist or nurse before taking Cresemba:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -if you have had an allergic reaction to other 'azole' anti-fungal treatments in the past, such as ketoconazole, fluconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole or posaconazole,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -if you are suffering from severe liver disease. Your doctor should monitor you for possible side effects.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Look out for side effects
texts.label: text

texts.text: Stop taking Cresemba and tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following side effects:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -sudden wheezing, difficulty breathing, swelling of the face, lips, mouth or tongue, severe itching, sweating, dizziness or fainting, fast heartbeat or pounding in the chest - these may be signs of a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis).
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Changes in your liver function
texts.label: text

texts.text: Cresemba can sometimes affect your liver function. Your doctor may carry out blood tests while you are taking this medicine.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Skin problems
texts.label: text

texts.text: Tell your doctor straight away if you get severe blistering of the skin, mouth, eyes or genitals.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Children and adolescents
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not give Cresemba capsules to children between the age of one year and 6 years, because this form of the medicine has not been tested in this age group. For children over 6 years and adolescents who wheigh at least 32 kg your doctor may prescribe Cresemba 100 mg capsules. Other forms of this medicine are more suitable for children or adolescents who cannot swallow capsules; ask your doctor or pharmacist.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Other medicines and Cresemba
texts.label: text

texts.text: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are using, have recently used or might use any other medicines. Some medicines may affect the way Cresemba works or Cresemba may affect the way they work, if they are taken at the same time.
texts.label: text

texts.text: In particular, do not take this medicine and tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking any of the following medicines:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -ketoconazole, used for fungal infections,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -high doses of ritonavir (more than 200 mg every 12 hours), used for HIV,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -rifampicin, rifabutin, used for tuberculosis,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -carbamazepine, used for epilepsy,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -barbiturate medicines like phenobarbital, used for epilepsy and sleep disorders,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -phenytoin, used for epilepsy,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -St John's wort, a herbal medicine used for depression,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -efavirenz, etravirine, used for HIV,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -nafcillin, used for bacterial infections.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Unless your doctor tells you otherwise, do not take this medicine and tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking any of the following medicines:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -rufinamide or other medicines which decrease the QT interval on the heart tracing (ECG),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -aprepitant, used to prevent nausea and vomiting by cancer treatment,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -prednisone, used for rheumatoid arthritis,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -pioglitazone, used for diabetes.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking any of the following medicines, as a dose adjustment or monitoring may be required to check that the medicines are still having the desired effect:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -ciclosporin, tacrolimus and sirolimus, used to prevent rejection of a transplant,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -cyclophosphamide, used for cancer,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -digoxin, used to treat heart failure or an uneven heart beat,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -colchicine, used for gout attack,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -dabigatran etexilate, used to stop blood clots after hip or knee replacement surgery,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -clarithromycin, used for bacterial infections,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -saquinavir, fosamprenavir, indinavir, nevirapine, lopinavir/ritonavir combination, used for HIV,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -alfentanil, fentanyl, used against strong pain,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -vincristine, vinblastine, used for cancer,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), used in transplant patients,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -midazolam, used for severe insomnia and stress,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -bupropion, used for depression,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -metformin, used for diabetes,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -daunorubicin, doxorubicin, imatinib, irinotecan, lapatinib, mitoxantrone, topotecan, used for different sorts of cancer.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Pregnancy and breast-feeding
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you are pregnant or breast-feeding, think you may be pregnant or are planning to have a baby, ask your doctor for advice before using this medicine.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not take Cresemba if you are pregnant, unless your doctor tells you otherwise. This is because it is not known if it may affect or harm your unborn baby.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not breast-feed if you are taking Cresemba.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Driving and using machines
texts.label: text

texts.text: Cresemba may make you feel confused, tired or sleepy. It can also make you pass out. Therefore, be very careful when driving or operating machinery.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Use in children and adolescents
texts.label: text

texts.text: The use of Cresemba 100 mg capsules in children and adolescents is not studied. Your doctor may give Cresemba 100 mg capsules to children and adolescents who weigh at least 32 kg.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Other forms of this medicine are suitable for children and adolsecents who cannot swallow capsules; ask your doctor or pharmacist.
texts.label: text

texts.text: You will take this dose until your doctor tells you otherwise. The duration of treatment with Cresemba may be longer than 6 months if your doctor considers this necessary.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Capsules can be taken with or without food. Swallow the capsules whole. Do not chew, crush, dissolve or open the capsules.
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you take more Cresemba than you should
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you take more Cresemba than you should, talk to a doctor or go to a hospital straight away. Take the medicine pack with you so the doctor knows what you have taken.
texts.label: text

texts.text: You may have more side effects such as:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -headache, feeling dizzy, restless or sleepy,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -tingling, reduced sense of touch or sensation in the mouth,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -problems being aware of things, hot flushes, anxiety, joint pain,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -changes in the way things taste, dry mouth, diarrhoea, vomiting,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -feeling your heart beat, faster heart rate, being more sensitive to light.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: If you forget to take Cresemba
texts.label: text

texts.text: Take the capsules as soon as you remember. However, if it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed dose.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not take a double dose to make up for a forgotten dose.
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you stop taking Cresemba
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not stop taking Cresemba unless you doctor has told you to do so. It is important to keep taking this medicine as long as your doctor tells you. This is to make sure that the fungal infection has gone.
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you have any further questions on the use of this medicine, ask your doctor, pharmacist or nurse.
texts.label: text

texts.text: 4. Possible side effects
texts.label: text

texts.text: Like all medicines, this medicine can cause side effects, although not everybody gets them.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Stop taking Cresemba and tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following side effects:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) such as sudden wheezing, breathing problems, swelling of the face, lips, mouth or tongue, severe itching, sweating, dizziness or fainting, fast heartbeat or pounding in the chest.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following side effects:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -severe blistering of the skin, mouth, eyes or genitals.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Other side effects
texts.label: text

texts.text: Tell your doctor, pharmacist or nurse if you notice any of the following side effects:
texts.label: text

texts.text: Common: may affect up to 1 in 10 people
texts.label: text

texts.text: -low potassium in your blood,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -decreased appetite,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -confusion (delirium),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -headache,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -sleepiness,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -inflamed veins that could lead to blood clots,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -shortness of breath or sudden and severe difficulty breathing,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -feeling sick (nausea), being sick (vomiting), diarrhoea, stomach pain,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -changes in blood tests of liver function,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -rash, itching,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -kidney failure (symptoms could include swelling of legs),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -chest pain, feeling tired or sleepy.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Uncommon: may affect up to 1 in 100 people
texts.label: text

texts.text: -reduced white blood cells - can increase your risk of infection and fever,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -reduced blood cells called 'platelets' - can increase your risk for bleeding or bruising,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -reduced red blood cells - can make you feel weak or short of breath or make your skin pale,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -severe reduction in blood cells - can make you feel weak, cause bruising or make infections more likely,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -rash, swelling of your lips, mouth, tongue or throat with difficulty breathing (hypersensitivity),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -low blood sugar levels,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -low blood levels of magnesium,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -low levels in the blood of a protein called 'albumin',
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -not getting the right goodness from your diet (malnutrition),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -low blood levels of sodium (hyponatraemia),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -depression, difficulty sleeping,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -seizure, fainting or feeling faint, dizziness,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -sensation of tingling, tickling, or pricking of the skin (paraesthesia),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -altered mental state (encephalopathy),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -changes in taste (dysgeusia),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -feeling of 'spinning' or being dizzy (vertigo),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -heart beat problems - may be too fast or uneven, or extra heart beats - this may show in your heart tracing (electrocardiogram or ECG),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -problems with the blood circulation,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -low blood pressure,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -wheezing, very fast breathing, coughing up blood or blood-stained sputum, nose bleeding,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -indigestion,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -constipation,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -feeling bloated (abdominal distension),
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -enlarged liver,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -inflammation of the liver,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -problems with the skin, red or purple spots on the skin (petechiae), inflamed skin (dermatitis), hair loss,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -back pain,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -swelling of the extremities,
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -feeling weak, very tired, or sleepy or generally out of sorts (malaise).
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Side effects with frequency not known:
texts.label: text

texts.text: -anaphylaxis (a severe allergic reaction).
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Reporting of side effects
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you get any side effects, talk to your doctor, pharmacist or nurse. This includes any possible side effects not listed in this leaflet. You can also report side effects directly via the national reporting system listed in Appendix V. By reporting side effects you can help provide more information on the safety of this medicine.
texts.label: text

texts.text: 5. How to store Cresemba
texts.label: text

texts.text: Keep this medicine out of the sight and reach of children.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not take this medicine after the expiry date which is stated on the label after EXP. The expiry date refers to the last day of that month.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not store above 30°C.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Store in the original packaging in order to protect from moisture.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not throw away any medicines via wastewater. Ask your pharmacist how to throw away medicines you no longer use. These measures will help protect the environment.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Scientific conclusions
texts.label: text

texts.text: Taking into account the PRAC Assessment Report on the PSUR(s) for isavuconazole, the scientific conclusions of PRAC are as follows:
texts.label: text

texts.text: In view of available data on hyponatraemia from clinical trials, the literature, spontaneous reports including 23 cases with a close temporal relationship, 11 cases with positive de-challenge and 1 case with positive re-challenge, the PRAC considers that a causal relationship between isavuconazole and hyponatraemia is at least a reasonable possibility. The PRAC concluded that the product information of products containing isavuconazole should be amended accordingly.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Having reviewed the PRAC recommendation, the CHMP agrees with the PRAC overall conclusions and grounds for recommendation.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Grounds for the variation to the terms of the marketing authorisation(s)
texts.label: text

texts.text: On the basis of the scientific conclusions for isavuconazole the CHMP is of the opinion that the benefit-risk balance of the medicinal product(s) containing isavuconazole is unchanged subject to the proposed changes to the product information
texts.label: text

texts.text: The CHMP recommends that the terms of the marketing authorisation(s) should be varied.
